title: Log Event Request
description: Request parameters for logging marketing events
x-tool-summary: Log batches of marketing events against a configured event source for measurement and attribution.

adcp_version.description: Release-precision AdCP version (VERSION.RELEASE, e.g. "3.0", "3.1", "3.1-beta"). On a request: the buyer's release pin — the seller validates against its supported_versions and returns VERSION_UNSUPPORTED on cross-major mismatch, or downshifts to the highest supported release within the same major. On a response: the release the seller actually served — clients SHOULD validate the response against that release's schema, not against their pin. Patches are not negotiated; surface them as build_version on capabilities for operational visibility. When omitted, falls back to adcp_major_version (deprecated) or server default. Buyers SHOULD emit both adcp_version and adcp_major_version through 3.x to remain compatible with sellers that only read the legacy field. NORMALIZATION: SDKs that read full-semver values from bundle metadata (e.g. ComplianceIndex.published_version = "3.1.0-beta.1") MUST normalize to release-precision ("3.1-beta.1") before emitting on the wire — meta-field values are NOT valid wire values.

adcp_major_version.description: DEPRECATED in favor of adcp_version (release-precision string). Servers MUST continue to honor this field through 3.x. Removed in 4.0. Original semantics: the AdCP major version the buyer's payloads conform to. Sellers validate against their supported major_versions and return VERSION_UNSUPPORTED if unsupported. When omitted, the seller assumes its highest supported version.

event_source_id.description: Event source configured on the account via sync_event_sources

test_event_code.description: Test event code for validation without affecting production data. Events with this code appear in the platform's test events UI.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated unique key for this request. Prevents duplicate event logging on retries. MUST be unique per (seller, request) pair to prevent cross-seller correlation. Use a fresh UUID v4 for each request.

external:core/version-envelope.json.title: AdCP Version Envelope
external:core/version-envelope.json.description: Release-precision AdCP protocol version negotiation fields. Composed via `allOf` into every AdCP request and response schema so the version semantics live in exactly one place. Distinct from `core/protocol-envelope.json`, which wraps responses at the transport layer (context_id / task_id / status / payload). This envelope is part of the payload itself.

external:core/event.json.title: Event
external:core/event.json.description: A marketing event (conversion, engagement, or custom) for attribution and optimization

event_id.description: Unique identifier for deduplication (scoped to event_type + event_source_id)

event_time.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event occurred

surface.description: Optional structured surface context for the event, such as an owned channel, profile, feed, podcast, newsletter list, website, app, or store. Complements `action_source`; use it when optimization-relevant meaning would otherwise live only in platform-specific `ext` metadata.

event_source_url.description: URL where the event occurred (required when action_source is 'website')

custom_event_name.description: Name for custom events (used when event_type is 'custom')

external:enums/event-type.json.title: Event Type
external:enums/event-type.json.description: Standard marketing event types for event logging, aligned with IAB ECAPI

enumDescriptions.view_content: User viewed specific content (product, article, etc.)
enumDescriptions.select_content: User selected or clicked on content (article, video, etc.)
enumDescriptions.select_item: User selected a specific product or item from a list
enumDescriptions.share: User shared content via social or messaging
enumDescriptions.add_to_cart: User added an item to cart
enumDescriptions.remove_from_cart: User removed an item from cart
enumDescriptions.add_to_wishlist: User added an item to a wishlist
enumDescriptions.refund: A purchase was fully or partially refunded (adjusts ROAS)
enumDescriptions.lead: User expressed interest (form submission, signup, etc.)
enumDescriptions.qualify_lead: Lead qualified by sales or scoring criteria
enumDescriptions.close_convert_lead: Lead converted to a customer or closed deal
enumDescriptions.disqualify_lead: Lead disqualified or marked as not viable
enumDescriptions.subscribe: User started a paid subscription or paid membership
enumDescriptions.follow: User made a free, durable opt-in to an account, channel, feed, list, podcast, or similar owned property
enumDescriptions.content_view: User meaningfully consumed a content unit, such as a watch, listen, stream, episode play, or read
enumDescriptions.watch_milestone: User reached a content progress threshold, such as 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, or a seconds-viewed milestone
enumDescriptions.schedule: User scheduled an appointment or event
enumDescriptions.submit_application: User submitted an application (loan, job, etc.)

external:core/user-match.json.title: User Match
external:core/user-match.json.description: User identifiers for attribution matching. Supports universal IDs, hashed identifiers, click IDs, and probabilistic matching.

uids.description: Universal ID values for user matching

hashed_email.description: SHA-256 hash of lowercase, trimmed email address. Buyer must normalize before hashing: lowercase, trim whitespace. Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — the email namespace is small enough that an unsalted SHA-256 is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries. Treat as PII for retention, consent, and access-control purposes. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.

hashed_phone.description: SHA-256 hash of E.164-formatted phone number (e.g. +12065551234). Buyer must normalize to E.164 before hashing. Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — the E.164 namespace is small enough that an unsalted SHA-256 is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries. Treat as PII for retention, consent, and access-control purposes. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.

click_id.description: Platform click identifier (fbclid, gclid, ttclid, ScCid, etc.)

click_id_type.description: Type of click identifier (e.g. fbclid, gclid, ttclid, msclkid, ScCid)

client_ip.description: Client IP address for probabilistic matching

client_user_agent.description: Client user agent string for probabilistic matching

external:enums/uid-type.json.title: UID Type
external:enums/uid-type.json.description: Type of user identifier. Used in audience sync, event logging, and TMP identity match requests to tell the receiver how to interpret and resolve the identifier; some types, including PAIR, are publisher-scoped rather than universal identity-graph tokens.

enumDescriptions.rampid: LiveRamp RampID maintained form (XY, 32 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.rampid_derived: LiveRamp RampID derived form (Xi, 48 bytes on the wire)
enumDescriptions.pairid: Publisher Addressable Identity via IAB Tech Lab PAIR. The OpenRTB profile uses User.eids[].source pair-protocol.com, EID.mm 3, EID.matcher set to the publisher's canonical ads.txt ownerdomain, and uids[].atype 3. The URL-safe Base64-encoded KsKp Publisher Identifier must be interpreted with that matcher scope. It is stable across a publisher's advertiser matches only within a Ks key epoch; Ks rotates every 30 days, and current and prior Publisher Identifiers can overlap during rollover. TMP identity objects do not carry matcher or ownerdomain, so a bridge requires an authenticated out-of-band binding to preserve PAIR scope.
enumDescriptions.hashed_email: SHA-256 hashed email address. Pseudonymous PII, not anonymous — unsalted SHA-256 of the email namespace is recoverable via precomputed dictionaries; treat as PII. See docs/reference/privacy-considerations#unsalted-hashed-identifiers-are-pseudonymous-not-anonymous.
enumDescriptions.publisher_first_party: Publisher's own first-party identifier, opaque to buyers
enumDescriptions.world_id_nullifier: World ID nullifier — a Sybil-resistant, relying-party-scoped, unlinkable pseudonym. Carries NO personhood or age assertion on its own; trust comes only from an accompanying verified `attestation`, never from this type tag. Distinct from the `world_id` value in the age-verification-method enum, which names a method, not an identifier.
enumDescriptions.other: Other universal ID type (specify in ext)

external:core/ext.json.title: Extension Object
external:core/ext.json.description: Extension object for platform-specific, vendor-namespaced parameters. Extensions are always optional and must be namespaced under a vendor/platform key (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization.

external:core/event-custom-data.json.title: Event Custom Data
external:core/event-custom-data.json.description: Event-specific data for attribution and reporting

value.description: Monetary value of the event. For an event source that declares value_currencies, currency is required and MUST appear in that list. Legacy sources without the new contract remain schema-compatible but are ineligible for canonical ROAS.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. For a source declaring value_currencies, monetary records MUST carry a currency from that list.

content_ids.description: Item identifiers for catalog attribution. Values are matched against catalog items using the identifier type declared by the catalog's content_id_type field (e.g., SKUs, GTINs, or vertical-specific IDs like job_id).

content_type.description: Category of content associated with the event (e.g., 'product', 'job', 'hotel'). Corresponds to the catalog type when used for catalog attribution.

content_name.description: Name of the product or content

content_category.description: Category of the product or content

num_items.description: Number of items in the event

progress_percent.description: Content progress percentage reached, primarily for `watch_milestone` events. Use 25, 50, 75, or 100 for quartiles, or another publisher-defined threshold. Do not use `value` for non-monetary progress.

progress_seconds.description: Content progress duration reached in seconds, primarily for `watch_milestone` events. Use when the milestone is time-based rather than percentage-based.

price.description: Price per unit of this item

enumDescriptions.app: Event occurred in a mobile or desktop app
enumDescriptions.phone_call: Event originated from a phone call
enumDescriptions.chat: Event originated from a chat conversation
enumDescriptions.email: Event originated from an email interaction
enumDescriptions.in_store: Event occurred at a physical retail location
enumDescriptions.system_generated: Event generated by an automated system

external:core/event-surface.json.title: Event Surface
external:core/event-surface.json.description: Structured context for the surface where an event source or logged event originated. Use this when the flat `action_source` is too coarse, such as a creator channel, social profile, podcast feed, newsletter list, or another owned platform property. `category` is a closed vocabulary so buyers can reason generically; `property_type` and `namespace` are open strings so new platforms and property shapes do not require a schema change. The flat `action_source` remains for backward compatibility. When `category` matches an ActionSource value, producers SHOULD set `action_source` to the same value. When `category` is `owned_property`, producers SHOULD keep the most compatible flat `action_source` for legacy consumers, commonly `system_generated` for platform-native events or `other` when no closer value applies.

category.description: Generic surface category. `owned_property` covers durable creator or brand-controlled properties hosted by a platform, such as channels, profiles, feeds, lists, podcasts, or playlists.

enumDescriptions.owned_property: Event occurred on or against a durable creator or brand-controlled platform property
enumDescriptions.app: Event occurred in a mobile or desktop app
enumDescriptions.offline: Event occurred offline or was imported from offline data
enumDescriptions.phone_call: Event originated from a phone call
enumDescriptions.chat: Event originated from a chat conversation
enumDescriptions.email: Event originated from an email interaction
enumDescriptions.in_store: Event occurred at a physical retail location
enumDescriptions.system_generated: Event was generated by an automated system

property_type.description: Open vocabulary describing the kind of property, for example `channel`, `profile`, `feed`, `list`, `podcast`, `playlist`, or `newsletter`. Required by convention when `category` is `owned_property`; optional for other categories.

namespace.description: Platform, publisher, or system namespace for the property, such as `video_platform`, `short_video_app`, `audio_service`, or a seller-defined namespace. This is intentionally not an enum.

property_id.description: Optional identifier for the property within `namespace`.

external:core/context.json.title: Context Object
external:core/context.json.description: Opaque correlation data that is echoed unchanged in responses. Used for internal tracking, UI session IDs, trace IDs, and other caller-specific identifiers that don't affect protocol behavior. Context data is never parsed by AdCP agents - it's simply preserved and returned.
